alternatives.description: Retain many separately scheduled Garden wake-ups.
alternatives.projected_effect: State-gated work remains correct but scheduled executions can overlap and increase transient concurrency/rate-limit pressure.
alternatives.risk: Too-many-requests failures can interrupt work and create unnecessary no-op invocations.

alternatives.description: Use one hourly ProcessEngine-bound Coordinator and absorb all former jobs as worker roles/due obligations.
alternatives.projected_effect: Garden work is serialized to one material unit per run, preserving the process roles while removing scheduled overlap.
alternatives.risk: Some multi-stage cycles take longer wall-clock time because independent reviews accumulate across runs.

bidirectional_gaps.gap: DO_NOTHING does not eliminate overlapping scheduler wake-ups or guarantee serialized provider use.
Serialization trades maximum throughput for lower concurrency pressure and may lengthen cycle completion time.

assumptions: The main observed failure mode is overlapping scheduled/agent work rather than a need for more independent scheduler lanes.
GardenProcessEngine@1 already separates process roles from authoritative route/state semantics.
Independent review quality can be preserved by accumulating blind family reviews across sequential Coordinator runs.
The user's instruction explicitly requests weekly-job removal and Process-Algebra-governed scheduling that avoids too-many-request pressure.
reason.uncertainty: Platform-side rate limits can still occur for reasons outside Garden, so the design reduces scheduled concurrency and fails closed on transient limits rather than claiming they are impossible.
counterexamples: If more than one Garden scheduler remains active, the serialization claim is false.
If the Coordinator launches parallel provider calls, rate-limit pressure can reappear despite one automation.
If a transient failure advances GardenProcess state, retry safety is broken.
If absorbed worker roles gain route/state authority outside ProcessFactory, the abstraction regresses.
reason.conclusion: Serialize Garden scheduling behind one hourly Coordinator, keep all roles as engine-bound worker/due obligations, disable the weekly brief, and fail closed without state advancement on transient rate limits.

obligations.statement: Repository schedule and binding manifest describe exactly one active Garden scheduler.
Former Garden jobs are absorbed/disabled rather than independently scheduled.
Transient 429/concurrency failure leaves GardenProcess state unchanged and defers retry.

items.claim_scope: Clean up active tasks, disable the weekly job, route scheduling through Process Algebra, and reduce too-many-request failures.
GardenProcessEngine@1 is the current shared route/state implementation.
Prior topology scheduled many Garden lanes independently.
